decisions.reason: The candidate already requires the latest reference as the primary model and similar reference-aligned messaging; the source changes the broader creative direction without necessarily changing its messaging constraints.
Using the latest reference as the video's model does not necessarily change the independent sourcing or testimonial presentation of the testimonial material.
The source decision changes creative modeling but does not change the Hindi-language requirements for the preview or final video.
Adapting the latest reference does not alter the specified 28–54 target audience or Indian-market context.
The source does not mention or negate the requirement for a naturally integrated call to action.
Selecting the latest reference as the direct creative model does not remove or modify the independently stated viral-style requirement.
The source does not change the requirement that the opening hook be direct and appropriate for the Indian audience.
The source selects the direction for full-video production after preview review but does not change the preview artifact, duration, language, or approval purpose.
The creative-direction change does not alter video count, duration, aspect ratios, or the pilot and follow-on ordering conditions.
Using the reference as a model does not transfer responsibility for script, visuals, or voiceover away from the freelancer.
The selected creative model does not change the conversion objective, CPL target, or priority of performance over aesthetics.
The decision to adapt the latest reference does not modify or remove the requirement for appropriate retention-focused cuts.
